claims.text: W-Ta-Mo-Nb-V is characterized as a Group IV-V transition-metal refractory high-entropy alloy family.
LMD or DMD can be used to fabricate the proposed W-Ta-Mo-Nb-V RHEA.
Substrate preheating improves compositional homogeneity during directed-energy deposition.
Preheating at 400-600°C reduces thermal gradients, residual stresses, and cracking.
Low-oxygen powders are beneficial for manufacturing refractory-metal high-entropy alloys.
The combined HIP treatment at 1100-1200°C and 100-150 MPa for 2-4 hours eliminates porosity and homogenizes the alloy.
Solution annealing at 1300-1400°C for 1-2 hours dissolves secondary phases.
Solution annealing reduces interstitial segregation at grain boundaries.
The LMD/DMD, HIP, and solution-annealing route enables structural integrity at temperatures up to 1000°C.
A single-phase BCC solid solution can be obtained in the proposed refractory-alloy family.
Single-phase BCC RHEAs with VEC below 4.5 are intrinsically ductile, whereas those with VEC at or above 4.6 are intrinsically brittle.
A VEC below 4.5 stabilizes the single-phase BCC structure.
Rapid solidification during LMD/DMD produces a fine-grained microstructure with grain size below 10 µm.
Reduced interstitial content and segregation enhance grain-boundary cohesion and dislocation mobility, thereby mitigating brittleness.
Suppressing brittle intermetallic phases mitigates the alloy's inherent brittleness.
The optimized alloy will have room-temperature yield strength above 800 MPa.
The optimized alloy will have room-temperature elongation above 10%.
The optimized alloy will retain more than 70% of its room-temperature strength at 1000°C.
The optimized alloy will have significantly greater fracture toughness than cast or conventionally processed counterparts.
Conventionally cast or sintered RHEAs generally have coarse grains, microsegregation, and high interstitial content that cause brittle fracture and poor high-temperature performance.

contradictions.description: An equiatomic W-Ta-Mo-Nb-V composition has a nominal VEC of about 5.4, not below 4.5. Thus the stated equiatomic or near-equiatomic target is inconsistent with the asserted VEC <4.5 applicability boundary and optimal mediator.

The target is described as a Group IV-V alloy, but W and Mo are Group VI elements and the stated W-Ta-Mo-Nb-V composition contains no Group IV element. The boundary also warns about Group VI additions while retaining W and Mo as principal target constituents.
